# Executive Summary
Statistical classification in R currently requires coordinating dozens of separate packages across data cleaning, diagnostic tests, model fitting, and evaluation. This fragmented workflow creates high technical barriers for students, educators, and applied researchers. This project unifies these disjointed tools into a single, production-grade open-source R package launched via run_app().

## Base MVP & Two-Stage Implementation
Development builds upon a fully functional interactive prototype featuring 8 workflow tabs and 6 supervised classification algorithms (LDA, QDA, 2-level/n-level Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Random Forests). Over six months, execution is structured into two stages:

**•	Stage 1.- Stabilization & Architecture (Months 1–3):** Refactor monolithic code into a 3-layer architecture (UI modules, moduleServer, and pure R functions), modernize the UI with bslib, integrate datamods, and design testthat suites.
**•	Stage 2.- Validation & Package Delivery (Months 4–6):** Execute end-to-end interface testing (shinytest2), resolve edge-case defects, conduct statistical verification of Discriminant Analysis calculations, enforce environment reproducibility via renv, and publish complete user documentation.

## Budget & Prior Investment
•	Requested Funding: $9,994.08 USD covering 282 hours of development labor across six months at an hourly rate of $35.44 USD/hour.
•	Prior Investment: Backed by ~720 hours of prior team labor ($21,600 USD value) that built the underlying functional prototype.

## Deliverables & Impact
The project will deliver a fully tested, GPL-3 licensed R package hosted on GitHub. By combining an intuitive graphical interface with underlying statistical rigour and reproducible environment locks (renv), the package lowers technical barriers and provides an accessible tool for education and reproducible research in R.
